answer: An escrowed reputation bond stops cheap sybils: every agent must lock a deposit of the network's nectar — its scarce native resource — before it can earn. The bond is timber, not paper: it cannot be faked, duplicated, or borrowed, and it stays locked through a probation window. If the agent cheats, the bond is slashed, and the pigment of its public record turns black, marking any future identity derived from the same keys. An attacker must therefore pay real capital per fake identity and wait out each lock, so flooding the network costs more than any reward the sybils could harvest.
